peopleAlsoAsk.question: Does karenia brevis cause red tide?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Red tide is one type of harmful algal bloom that is caused by high concentrations of toxic dinoflagellates, microscopic algae. In Florida and the Gulf of Mexico, the alga that causes most red tides is Karenia brevis, often abbreviated as K. brevis.
peopleAlsoAsk.title: Red Tide | Water Quality Dashboard - Protecting Florida Together

peopleAlsoAsk.question: What causes excessive growth of algae and results in algal bloom?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus cause an overgrowth of algae in a short period of time, also called algae blooms. The overgrowth of algae consumes oxygen and blocks sunlight from underwater plants. When the algae eventually dies, the oxygen in the water is consumed.
peopleAlsoAsk.title: The Effects: Dead Zones and Harmful Algal Blooms | US EPA
